sides.text: Entry point returns int; #include <stdio.h> declares printf
Sizes are platform-defined; char is 1 byte by definition
sides.code: printf("%zu %zu %zu %zu\n", sizeof(char), sizeof(int), sizeof(long), sizeof(double));

sides.text: Unsigned arithmetic wraps; fixed-width types in <stdint.h>
sides.code:
int32_t a = -5; uint8_t b = 250; b += 10;
printf("%d %u\n", a, b);

sides.text: Division truncates toward zero; % takes the dividend's sign
Precedence: * before +, shifts before &, == before &; avoid modifying a variable twice in one expression
No bounds checking; unspecified elements are zero

sides.code:
char s[] = "abc";
printf("%zu %zu %c\n", sizeof s, strlen(s), s[3] == 0 ? '0' : 'x');

sides.text: strcat/strcpy can overflow; prefer strncat or snprintf
Adding n advances n elements, not n bytes
Function parameters lose the array size
Every malloc needs one free; check for NULL
calloc zero-fills; realloc may move the block
Useful for out-parameters and arrays of strings
const int * : data read-only. int * const : pointer fixed
Dot for values, arrow for pointers
The compiler aligns members; order fields large to small
sides.code:
struct S { char c; int i; char d; };
printf("%zu %zu\n", sizeof(struct S), (size_t)((char*)&((struct S*)0)->i - (char*)0));

sides.text:
Set: x |= 1<<n
clear: x &= ~(1<<n)
toggle: x ^= 1<<n
Signed overflow, out-of-bounds, use after free, and uninitialized reads are all undefined
restrict promises no overlap so the compiler can optimize
Needs a count or sentinel; arguments are not type-checked

static at file scope hides a name
inside a function it persists. extern declares
register is a hint
sides.code:
static int hits;
hits++;

unsigned x = 1;
printf("%s\n", *(unsigned char *)&x ? "little" : "big");

#define T(x) _Generic((x), int: "int", double: "double", default: "other")
printf("%s %s\n", T(1), T(1.5));

sides.text: Pack fields into bits; layout is implementation-defined
volatile prevents optimizing away reads and writes (hardware registers); it is not a thread-safety tool. Use <stdatomic.h>
sides.code:
volatile int flag = 0;
flag = 1;

sides.text: = vs ==, string literals are read-only, sizeof on a pointer
Arguments are passed by value; declare before use or use a prototype
Parenthesize arguments and body; arguments may be evaluated twice
Comparator takes const void *; subtraction can overflow
